# moddotplot-interactive v0.8.3

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

v0.8.3 makes multi-sequence grids read in the same genomic X/Y convention as an opened
interactive comparison and allows the displayed sequence order to be rearranged in
place. It also simplifies the genomic window-size readout. These interface changes do
not alter the estimator or the numeric contents of generated matrix cells.

See the [validation record](v0.8.3/VALIDATION.md) for the completed local verification
evidence.

## Grid orientation and comparison ordering

The X axis follows the selected sequence order from left to right, while the Y axis
uses that same order from bottom to top. Self-similarity plots consequently run from
the bottom-left cell to the top-right cell. Each off-diagonal preview represents its
column sequence on X and row sequence on Y; the reciprocal cell is a true transposed
rendering of the same computed pair.

Opening any grid cell preserves those displayed axis assignments in the interactive
view. This corrects the former reciprocal-cell placement in which the upper-right and
bottom-left representations could appear under the wrong X/Y ordering.

## Reorderable grid axes

Every grid sequence label now exposes a reorder handle. A sequence can be dragged from
either axis to a new position, and keyboard users can reorder a focused handle with the
corresponding axis arrow keys. Because X and Y are two views of one shared sequence
order, a move updates both axes together and keeps the self plots on the anti-diagonal.

Reordering only rearranges the completed labels and canvases. It does not rerun the
self or pairwise comparisons, so the bounded grid computation and memory model remain
unchanged.

## Single-value plot window size

**Plot window size** now reports one nearest-whole-base value per cell. Uneven genomic
partitions no longer appear as a one-base floor-to-ceiling range such as
`32,540–32,541 bp per cell`; the cleaned readout presents a single representative
value instead. Zoom, reset, and sequence changes continue to update it from the current
genomic domain and scientific plot resolution.
